The server can load the same file without reporting it.
documents.s: Warnings that do not stop loading

documents.t: Write both forms at the root when a requirement must be enforced by the server and shown in the client UI. The server reads only prerequisite; the client reads preSkill and preSkillLevel, and does not read prerequisite. Use the same vnum and level in both forms. name: example_cleave type: CLASS maxLevel: 20 prerequisite: { vnum: 1, level: 10 } preSkill: 1 preSkillLevel: 10 resolve: by: server per_compute: - type: DAMAGE amountPoly: '100+60*skill_k' damageType: MELEE Add the client metadata, flags, cost, and range appropriate to the skill. The flat keys set the requirement UI; they do not enforce the server requirement.
documents.s: A prerequisite visible in the client

documents.t: This passive applies an affect when its holder mounts and turns off on dismount. An affect is a timed or persistent status on a character. NO_MANUAL_USE removes the manual-use button; NO_COOLDOWN permits a trigger on each mount. name: example_mounted_bonus type: PASSIVE maxLevel: 20 triggersOn: - event: RIDE triggersOff: - event: UNRIDE flags: [NO_COOLDOWN, NO_MANUAL_USE] client: job: HORSE icon: skill/common/horse/charge resolve: by: server per_compute: - type: AFFECT point: MOB_CRITICAL_PCT amountPoly: 'min(10, skill_level)' durationPoly: '3600' The affect has its own duration; choose one that fits the intended behavior. See Collect, accept and triggers for trigger conditions and events.

A node does nothing and the log is quiet. A key a node type does not read is ignored. For example, nodes: on POISON and successPctPoly on TICKER have no effect. Check the node reference. An ordered search collects nothing. A collect.search with order: also needs take:. With an order, zero iterations collect nothing; without an order, zero means unbounded. AUTO_SHOOT targets are exempt because targetCountPoly supplies the count. An 80 percent success chance fires only 8 percent of the time. successPctPoly uses per mille: use '800' for 80 percent. Omitting the key makes the node always succeed. A one-shot ticker fails validation. delayPoly is required even when countPoly is 1. Give it the same value as delayStartPoly. An attached ticker ends before its final tick. If its affect duration and final tick fall in the same pulse, the affect can end first and stop the run. Leave headroom or omit the affect duration. A decal is half the blast's size. width is a diameter; search.radius is a radius. A radius of 1000 needs a width of 2000. post_preflight: never runs. Triggered casts run per_use: and per_compute: only. A client-resolved cast also needs the end-of-motion packet to reach post_preflight:; there is no timeout for a missing packet. Put effects required for a paid cast in per_use:. An effect runs once per victim instead of once per cast. per_compute: runs per seed. For a value based on the total use.victims, use post_preflight: when its completion rules fit the skill. A passive trigger never fires. Only type: PASSIVE keeps triggersOn; other types drop it without a message. A trigger with no cooldown can fire on every matching event. The client and server disagree about a requirement. Keep root prerequisite.vnum and prerequisite.level aligned with root preSkill and preSkillLevel. The server enforces the former; the client uses the latter for its UI. The server does not read the client: block.

Skill file and glossary: setup, top-level keys, and phases. Skill nodes: node types and required keys. Collect, accept and triggers: target selection and event conditions. Skill descriptions: description variables and validation. One file per skill: the model behind the file.

A skill extension binds Lua functions to a skill node. Use a handler to filter targets, change a damage intent before defense, or act after an affect is added. For the terms used here, see the Skills glossary; for the model, see Beyond the formula.

In conf/skill/100.ucskill.yaml, add a handler name to a DAMAGE node: - type: DAMAGE id: damage amountPoly: '100*skill_k' damageType: MELEE handler: example_cleave accept: of: ENEMY In conf/skill/100.lua, return a table with that name: local M = {} ---@type DamageNodeHandler M.example_cleave = { damage_intent = function(intent) if intent:is_back_hit(35) then intent.attack = math.floor(intent.attack * 1.3) end end, } return M The handler increases the attack for a back hit before defense is subtracted. The YAML excerpt is a node in a skill's phase list, not a complete skill file; see the skill file reference for the surrounding file.

Item Location or shape Purpose Skill file conf/skill/<vnum>.ucskill.yaml A node declares handler: <name>. Handler module conf/skill/<vnum>.lua Returns a table keyed by handler name. Handler annotations Quest metadata stubs Define DamageIntent, AffectAppliedCtx, DamageNodeHandler, and AffectNodeHandler for the language server. The skill file and module share a folder and vnum, the numeric skill identifier. The loader reads the module once per skill and stores its table in SKILL_EXTENSIONS[vnum]. Each call looks up the function there again. Nodes in any phase, including nested nodes, can name handlers; multiple nodes can share a name. Policy variants use the same module. Annotate a handler with ---@type DamageNodeHandler or ---@type AffectNodeHandler to check its slot signatures against the stubs. A handler table must contain at least one recognized function.

Slot Signature Return When it runs gate gate(intent) Boolean; false skips the node for the target Before the node acts on each collected target in the per-target loop. damage_intent damage_intent(intent) Ignored For a DAMAGE node, after formula and scaling, before defense. applied applied(ctx) Ignored For an AFFECT node, after the affect is added. Omitted slots do nothing. A slot on an incompatible node type is not called. Place effects that bypass the per-target loop do not call gate. Dead or stunned targets do not reach the gate. A gate receives a DamageIntent with only caster, victim, and skill populated. Its numeric fields are 0 and ignore_defense is false. Return true explicitly to let the node proceed: local M = {} ---@type DamageNodeHandler M.example_gate = { gate = function(intent) return intent:is_back_hit(35) end, } return M A damage_intent function changes the object in place. The engine reads that same object after the call. An applied function receives read-only context and runs only if the affect was added. For example, a stronger good affect of the same type and point can cause the node to return before the callback.

DamageIntent is created for each gate or damage_intent call. Field Type Access Meaning caster LPCHARACTER Read-only The attacker. victim LPCHARACTER Read-only The target. skill integer Read-only The skill vnum. attack integer Writable Attack before defense; 0 in a gate. type integer Writable The hit's EDamageType. ignore_defense boolean Writable Skip flat defense subtraction. damage_attribute integer Writable The SKILL_DAMAGE_ATTR_* bits. intent:is_back_hit(deg) returns whether the angle between caster and victim rotations is less than deg degrees. A value of 0 or less uses 35 degrees. It returns false if either character is missing. The damage handler runs after the amount formula, battle damage calculation, splash factor, ability_scaling, and ranged bow distance falloff. Defense and later damage modifiers consume the edited fields afterward. Use math.floor when assigning a fractional calculation to attack.

AffectAppliedCtx is passed to applied. Its fields are read-only. Field Type Meaning caster LPCHARACTER The caster, if present. victim LPCHARACTER The target carrying the added affect. skill integer The skill vnum. affect integer The affect type added. duration integer Duration in seconds.

A DAMAGE node can declare ability_scaling to scale its attack using points on the caster and victim. Use point names defined by your host: ability_scaling: { adder: EXAMPLE_ADDER, resist: EXAMPLE_RESIST } Key Point read from adder Caster resist Victim After the splash factor, the engine uses integer arithmetic: attack = max(0, attack * (100 + caster[adder] - victim[resist]) / 100) The clamp to 0 applies to every DAMAGE node. Without the field, or when a point name does not resolve, the corresponding points read as 0. An unknown point name does not produce a log line. Check both names against the host's point list.

Extension Interface Use Node handler Lua module named by the skill vnum Gate a target, edit a damage intent, or react to an added affect. ability_scaling YAML field on a DAMAGE node Apply the adder and resist calculation. Skill-bound trait traits: on a node Bind behavior with the lifetime of an affect. See the traits reference. Node type Native registration and implementation Add a kind of node action. There are 24 live node types. Handlers are Lua functions; there is no native handler registration. A Lua handler cannot add a node type. An intracore skill, which runs on each core without a performer, cannot declare a handler because there is no caster to pass to it.

Handlers run synchronously in the combat path through a protected call. They cannot yield or wait. A gate runs once per collected target, not once per cast. A gate error is logged and the node runs. A gate that returns nothing is read as false and skips the node. Errors in damage_intent and applied are logged; the hit or affect continues. Changes made to an intent before an error remain in place. Make calls that can fail before writing the fields. Handler state is scoped to the call unless you explicitly store it elsewhere. For behavior tied to an affect's lifetime, see the traits reference. A handler load fault does not stop the core; the affected handler is unavailable. Invalid skill YAML can prevent the skill table from initializing.

Log line Cause or result skill {} declares a handler but {} is missing The module for the skill vnum is missing. skill {} extension load error: {} The module failed to compile or raised a top-level error. skill {} {}.lua must return a table of handlers The module did not return a table. skill {} handler '{}' not found in {}.lua The named handler is not a key of the returned table. skill {} handler '{}' implements none of gate, damage_intent or applied The handler has no recognized function. skill {} gate error: {} The gate failed; the node runs. skill {} damage_intent error: {} The callback failed; the hit continues. skill {} applied error: {} The callback failed; the affect remains. Skill[{}] {}: node {} declares `handler:`; an intracore cast has no caster to hand it An intracore skill declares a handler; loading is refused.

A misspelled slot beside a valid slot loads without the "implements none" error. Test each callback. A gate cannot inspect the computed attack: its numeric intent fields are 0. Use damage_intent for a rule based on the hit. has_affect takes a numeric affect id, while has_affect_flag and get_affect_value take names. A type error aborts the callback; earlier intent edits remain. damage_intent only runs on DAMAGE nodes and applied only on AFFECT nodes. The loader does not check slot compatibility with the node type.
A skill file defines a skill's costs, targeting, presentation, and effect nodes. The server and client read the same YAML file. For the model behind it, see Skills.

Save this example as conf/skill/1.ucskill.yaml and make the same file available to the client: name: example_cleave type: CLASS maxLevel: 40 costType: SP costPoly: '40' cooldownPoly: '15' range: 450 flags: [ENEMYONLY, ATTACK_SKILL, NEED_TARGET] client: job: WARRIOR icon: skill/example_cleave motionIndex: 1 resolve: by: client bound: { targets: '5', hitsPerTarget: '1' } per_compute: - type: DAMAGE id: damage amountPoly: '100' damageType: MELEE accept: { of: ENEMY } Supply an icon and a motion that sends skill hits in your client. The server accepts up to five distinct targets and one hit per target for a cast; each accepted hit runs the damage node. See descriptions for the player-facing name and tooltip.

Term Meaning Policy A registered rule or variant selected for a skill. Handle An identifier returned when a rule is registered, used to refer to that registration. Vnum The numeric identifier of a skill. Poly A formula string evaluated using named values. Intracore A cast authorized on one core and executed on every core without a performer. Subject The character, guild, or empire that owns a cast. Anchor The position or entity used as a reference for a node's target search. Node An effect in a phase or in another node's children. Phase A list of nodes run at a particular point in a cast. Core A running game server process.

Item Location or purpose Skill file conf/skill/<vnum>.ucskill.yaml, one file per vnum. The filename supplies the vnum; there is no root vnum key. Handler conf/skill/<vnum>.lua, for handlers named by nodes. See extensions. Policy IDs conf/skill/policies.yaml declares IDs accepted under policies. Description desc declares variables; client description files provide the text. See descriptions. The server ignores names without the .ucskill.yaml suffix. Deploy the same skill files to the client pack at locale/universal/skill. The client looks for vnums 1 through 1000; a character can hold skill vnums up to 399. The server reads the folder as a whole at boot and on a proto reload. A boot load failure stops initialization; a failed reload keeps the old table. See errors and examples.
Root keys are optional except for resolve. Values under client are presentation fields. A poly is a formula, and quoted strings keep YAML from interpreting the expression as another type.

Key Type Meaning name string Internal name, up to 64 characters, also used in logs. Player-facing text comes from the description file. type enum CLASS, SPECIALIZATION, HORSE, SUPPORT, GUILD, PASSIVE, or MOB. An unknown value is logged and becomes no type. PASSIVE enables triggersOn; the client uses HORSE to identify a horse skill. maxLevel integer Highest skill level. levelLimit integer Character level required by the server. prerequisite map Server requirement: {vnum: <skill>, level: <n>}. The server enforces this field. preSkill, preSkillLevel integers Flat root fields read by the client to show its requirement UI. For a requirement that must also appear in that UI, write both these fields and the matching prerequisite map. The client does not read prerequisite; the server enforces only prerequisite. subject enum Cast owner: character, guild, or empire. Defaults to guild for type: GUILD, otherwise character. An unknown value fails loading. intracore boolean Authorize on the originating core and execute on every core without a performer. Requires a guild or empire subject.

Key Type Meaning costType enum SP, HP, or SUBJECT_GOLD. Absent or empty means no cost; costPoly is then not read. costPoly poly Cost amount. cooldownPoly poly Cooldown in seconds. Cost and cooldown are evaluated before a victim is hit, with caster values. The client evaluates them too. SUBJECT_GOLD charges the guild or empire subject; it is invalid for a character subject. SP and HP costs are invalid for guild and empire subjects.

Key Type Meaning range integer Use range. 0 is unbounded. range_bonus point name The point value multiplied by 100 extends server reach. An unknown name fails loading. useTimeout integer How long a use stays in flight, in milliseconds; also the charge windup window. weaponLimitation list SWORD, DAGGER, BOW, TWO_HANDED, BELL, FAN, or DOUBLE_SWORD, an alias of DAGGER. Empty or absent allows any weapon. Invalid entries are logged. shoot boolean The hit arrives on a shoot packet. charge boolean The press starts a dash and arrival lands the hit, within useTimeout. skillshot boolean Client-side motion hitbox targeting without a distance check. The server allows range + 300, plus range_bonus * 100, for latency slack. Range gates a use; it does not collect targets. A splash has its own radius. A charge requires an AFFECT node that raises TANHWAN_DASH; that affect also requires charge: true. Put the dash in per_use. See nodes.

resolve: by: client bound: { targets: '5', hitsPerTarget: '1' } Key Meaning by Required: server selects victims, or client supplies them through hit packets. Missing or unknown values fail loading. bound.targets Poly limiting distinct victims per cast. 0 or empty is unbounded. bound.hitsPerTarget Poly limiting hits per victim. 0 or empty is unbounded. The bound limits client claims at the entry point. A node can also have its own ledger limit; see collect, accept, and triggers. With server resolution the bound is still evaluated and use.bound.targets can read it.

Write flags as a list under flags. Unknown names are logged and skipped; an absent list sets no flags. Flag Read by Meaning SELFONLY, OTHERONLY, NPCONLY, PCONLY Server Restrict the victim of a use. ALLYONLY, ENEMYONLY Both Restrict the victim; the client also avoids offering the wrong target. NPC_BUFF Both Allow an NPC target if its AI accepts buffs. TOGGLE Server Mark a toggle and relax duration checks for AFFECT and AUTO_SHOOT. NO_COOLDOWN Server Do not apply a cooldown after use. PERSISTENT_COOLDOWN Server Keep cooldown across relog. TARGET_TRIGGER_SUBJECT Server Aim a triggered cast at the event's other party. ATTACK_SKILL Both Mark an attack and enforce attack restrictions. LEVEL_UP_BY_POINT Both Allow raising the skill with a point. NO_MANUAL_USE Client Do not offer manual casting. This is separate from type: PASSIVE. NEED_TARGET, SEARCH_TARGET, NEED_CORPSE, CAN_USE_FOR_ME, CAN_CHANGE_DIRECTION, STANDING_SKILL, MOVING_SKILL, AFFECT_TOGGLED, FAN_RANGE, CIRCLE_RANGE Client Control how the interface turns a press into a cast. Victim flags govern the target of a use. A node's accept filters the targets that node reaches.

Key Meaning triggersOn, triggersOff Trigger configuration. See collect, accept, and triggers. desc Description variables under vars. Invalid entries fail loading. See descriptions. policies Map of policy IDs to paths and values patched onto a copy of the skill. Each ID must be declared in policies.yaml. Policies resolve in registration order. per_use, per_compute, post_preflight Phase lists containing nodes. There is no root nodes list. Put nodes in a phase; a node may also contain child nodes.

Key Meaning job Skill list: WARRIOR, ASSASSIN, SURA, SHAMAN, SPEC, RAGE, ACTIVE, SUPPORT, GUILD, HORSE, PASSIVE, or NONE. Case does not matter. An unknown value makes the client drop the skill. icon Path under the image root. motionIndex Motion; an empty string means no motion. gradeCount Number of grade variants; default 4. minPgLevel Character level required by the interface. motionLoopCount Poly for the motion loop count. The client also reads root fields including range, range_bonus, skillshot, costs, cooldown, maxLevel, flags, weapon limitations, charge, type, subject, preSkill, preSkillLevel, desc, policies, and resolve.bound.targets. A mob skill can omit client.

An intracore cast has no performer. The loader rejects these shapes: Refused shape Reason character subject Character state is not present on every core. per_use It needs a caster seed. No per_compute nodes There is no effect to execute. Top-level node without collect.search, or with collect.from, collect.origin, collect.scalePoly, or a caster source There is no seed or performer to supply a center. Top-level node with of: SELF, of: PARTY, or without explicit ALLY or ENEMY The relation needs a performer or roster side. handler, damageType: RANGE, absorb, or to: caster Each requires a performer's body. post_preflight remains available. For target selection, see collect, accept, and triggers.

Each phase is an optional sequence. Node IDs share a counter across phases, so a poly in one phase can refer to a node in another. Phase When it runs Seed per_use Once per cast, before computation. Caster. Its nodes can still search for other targets. per_compute Once per seed. One victim. Resolution determines how seeds arrive. post_preflight Once after all victims are known. Caster. use.victims is available here. With resolve.by: server, traversal runs per_compute and then post_preflight. With resolve.by: client, each accepted hit packet runs per_compute; the end-of-motion packet runs post_preflight. The server counts victims in its own ledger. A triggered cast runs per_use and per_compute once and does not run post_preflight. A client hit packet is checked for resolution mode, a prior press, polymorph, victim flags, a victim, range, and the resolve bound. For node types and child execution, see nodes; for failures, see errors and examples.

A node describes one effect in a skill phase or in another node's nodes: list. The server supports 24 live node types. For terms such as node, affect, and poly (a formula string), see the skill file glossary. For the model and phases, see Nodes and phases. This node applies damage and then attempts to slow each collected victim: - type: DAMAGE id: bolt amountPoly: 100+2*calc_raw_phys_att*skill_k damageType: MAGIC successPctPoly: '800' nodes: - type: SLOW amountPoly: '30' durationPoly: '5' A child runs once for each victim the parent collected, seeded with that victim, and runs its own collect: from there. It is "for each of mine, do this", not "then also do this". Traversal descends into children only when the parent's own step returned true. What false means is per type: a failed success roll, a rejected target, a horse skill meeting a player.

Key Meaning type Required. An unknown or retired name fails the file. id Optional name. It is what node.<id>.<stat> and desc.vars refs address, and what names the node's collection ledger. It must be unique in the file, across all three phases. collect:, accept: Who the node reaches. See Collect, accept and targets. targets: AUTO_SHOOT and CONCATENATED_ATTACK only, where it is mandatory. nodes: Children. Read only on the types marked in the table below; on the others it is ignored. handler: Names a table in the skill's Lua file. See Handlers. successPctPoly A per-mille roll: the node runs when a random number from 1 to 1000 is at most the poly. Absent means it always succeeds. Only on the types marked below. '800' is 80 percent. stopOnCasterDeath Only on the timed types. Whether the caster's death ends the run. upkeep:, attach:, traits:, counters: Only on the types that raise an affect. See Nodes that raise an affect.

Type Children Success roll Raises an affect Timed DAMAGE yes yes HEAL yes yes AFFECT yes yes yes CRUSH yes PULL yes yes TICKER yes yes yes AUTO_SHOOT yes yes yes CONCATENATED_ATTACK yes yes COLLECTOR yes FIRE, BLEEDING, POISON, STUN, SLOW yes REMOVE_GOOD_AFFECT, REMOVE_BAD_AFFECT, REMOVE_BLEEDING yes CUT_POINT yes SPECIFIC_EFFECT, POINT_CHANGE, TAUNT AMBIENCE_EFFECT, GROUND_DECAL, IMPACT_EFFECT

AFFECT, TICKER and AUTO_SHOOT all put an affect on someone, so all three take these keys. upkeep: point: SP amountPoly: '10' counters: damage_taken: { event: DAMAGE_TAKEN, from: CASTER } Key Meaning affect The affect flag the node sets. affectVnum The identity of the affect. Default is the skill vnum. See Traits reference for binding identity. upkeep What the affect drains per tick while it holds. point is SP or HP (HP also marks the affect as costing health), amountPoly is required. An unknown point or a missing amount fails the file. attach TICKER and AUTO_SHOOT: affect gives the run and the affect one lifetime. It takes only the word affect. traits A list of { id:, constants:, formulas:, params: }. The behavior this affect gates. See Traits reference. counters A map of name to { event:, from: }: running totals the affect keeps. event is one of DAMAGE_TAKEN, DAMAGE_DEALT, HEAL_TAKEN, HEAL_DONE, DEBUFF_TAKEN, DEBUFF_GIVEN, KILL, DIED. from is ANY (default), CASTER, PC or NON_PC. At most 8 counters per node. Read a total as node.<id>.<name>. Inside a traits: entry, constants are polys in the node's own names, evaluated per holder. formulas are polys in the trait's names, stored on the binding. params map a name to an enum value, and the name must end in _point (a point), _column (a mob resist column) or _affect (an affect flag) to say which enum it reads. trait: in the singular, and constants, formulas or params outside a traits: entry, are errors. More on affects is in Affects reference.

Key Meaning amountPoly Required. The attack value before defence. damageType Required. NORMAL or TRUE_DAMAGE (the same thing, ignores flat defence), MELEE, RANGE, MAGIC, SPECIALISTIC, SPECIAL. damageAttribute ` penetratePctPoly Per-mille roll. On success the hit ignores defence. ignoreTargetAttRatingPoly Per-mille roll. ability_scaling { adder:, resist: } point names. The damage is multiplied by 100 + caster adder - victim resist percent, floored at 0. A type: HORSE skill returns false against a player before any of it. Records damage.
Key Meaning amountPoly Required. Scaled by the splash modifier. Records heal.

Key Meaning point The point the affect moves. Optional: without it the affect is a pure flag. A name no point matches fails the file. amountPoly Defaults to '0'. Scaled by the splash modifier. durationPoly Seconds. 0 is an infinite affect. Required unless the skill has TOGGLE, and always required on a child node. affect, affectVnum See above. affect_class List of affect macros this node's affect joins: IS_GOOD_AFFECT, IS_DISPELLABLE_AFFECT, IS_PARTY_BUFF_AFFECT, IS_UNTARGETABLE_AFFECT and the rest. Per node, so one skill can carry a good buff node and a bad debuff node. absorb Also apply -amount to the caster, with absorbAffect as its flag, unless the caster already carries that vnum and point. setSource Stamp the caster's id on the affect. A status effect has its own node type: point: STUN is not how a node stuns.
Key Meaning amountPoly Required knockback distance. Pushes away from the caster and stops at walls.

Key Meaning amountPoly Required. Pulls the victim toward the node's centre, never past it. collect.origin moves the centre. Only players other than the caster are eligible; otherwise the step returns false.

Re-runs its children on the same victim, on a clock. Key Meaning countPoly How many ticks. Required unless attach: affect, where the affect ending is the other way out. delayPoly Required, always, even for a single tick. Seconds between ticks. delayStartPoly Seconds before the first tick. Default 0.1. durationPoly The attached affect's own lifetime. Empty means as long as the ticks last. cooldownAfterEnd Start the skill's cooldown after the last tick instead of at the cast. stopOnCasterDeath Default false. anchor position freezes the seed's place at plant time and re-enters the subtree there. The victim becomes irrelevant: it may die, warp or log out and the subtree still runs. affect, affectVnum, attach, upkeep, traits, counters See above. A ticker needs at least one child. anchor: position cannot be combined with attach: affect. An affect, affectVnum or durationPoly without attach: affect is an error. node.<id>.iteration is 1 on the first tick. With attach: affect the lifetime is two-way: a dispel, a cleanse or the caster leaving stops the run, and the run ending removes the affect.

A toggle that fires at a fresh search every interval. Key Meaning fly Required. The projectile. affect Required. The affect flag the toggle raises on its holder. intervalPoly Required. Seconds between shots, evaluated every tick. targetCountPoly Required. How many targets one tick takes, evaluated every tick. Write a fixed count as a constant poly. durationPoly Run length. 0 or empty is infinite. Required unless the skill has TOGGLE, and always required on a child node. targets: Required, with a collect.search. Who the shots hunt. The node's own collect: and accept: say who holds the toggle, normally the caster. The run and its affect share one lifetime whether or not attach: is written. stopOnCasterDeath defaults to true. At least one child is required.

A chain that jumps from victim to victim. Key Meaning fly Required. maxTarget Required, above 0. Total hops. targets: Required, with a collect.search. targets.accept.ledger.max_per_victim is how many times one victim may be hit again; 0 is unbounded. Live branches of one chain are capped at 64: take: 3 over five generations would be 243 leaves, and a typo must not take a core down. stopOnCasterDeath defaults to true. At least one child is required. Inside a child, node.<id>.iteration counts the hop.

Does nothing itself. It owns a collect: and accept: that several children share: one search, one budget, one ledger. Its step always returns true, so traversal reaches its children for each collected victim. Key Meaning collect, accept, nodes Shared population and children; see the common keys above.
Key Meaning point Required point name. An unknown name fails the file. to caster or victim (default). amountPoly Required. Records amount. Write to:, not on:; YAML 1.1 treats on as a boolean.
Key Meaning to caster (default) or center. Directs a monster or boss toward that target. On other victims it does nothing and returns true.
Key Meaning point HP or SP only. amountPoly Required; subtracted from the victim. Records cut. absorb Add the same amount to the caster. fly Projectile drawn from victim to caster with absorb.
Key Meaning amountPoly Damage amount. An empty value loads but deals nothing. tickAmountPoly Default '5'. tickFrequencyPoly Default '3'.
Key Meaning amountPoly Required damage amount. tickAmountPoly Default '5'. tickFrequencyPoly Default '3'.
Key Meaning successPctPoly Optional success roll; see common keys.
Key Meaning durationPoly Required duration. ignoreImmune Bypass the immunity check when true.
Key Meaning amountPoly Required. The movement speed change is -amount plus the caster's slow adder. durationPoly Required duration. ignoreImmune Bypass the immunity check when true.
Key Meaning successPctPoly Optional success roll; see common keys.
Key Meaning successPctPoly Optional success roll; see common keys.
Key Meaning removeDispel Default true; false skips dispel-curse affects. removeCleansable Default true; false skips the cleansable walk, leaving only poison and fire eligible for removal.
Key Meaning effectPath Required. The effect file. bone Where it attaches. Empty means the root bone.

AMBIENCE_EFFECT, GROUND_DECAL and IMPACT_EFFECT act on a place, not on a victim. They run once per collected victim, at that victim's place, and once at the node's own centre when nobody was collected, which is the case they exist for. Under a COLLECTOR the centre is each victim's position. Under a TICKER with anchor: position it is the anchor. A centre with no map is not a location, and the node plants nothing.
Key Meaning effectPath Required server-owned effect. soundPath Optional sound. ttlPoly Required lifetime in seconds.

Key Meaning shape CIRCLE, CONE, or RECTANGLE. CUSTOM fails the file. width, height Full extents in world units; default 300. rotation Degrees; with attach: victim, an offset from the victim's facing. outlinePct 0 fills the shape; above 0 draws a band inside the edge. coneAngle Cone half-angle in degrees; default 45. color 0xAARRGGBB; default 0x80FF0000. ttlPoly Required lifetime. timerPoly Client countdown; 0 means none. attach victim follows the character the centre came from.

Key Meaning rangePoly Required viewer distance gate; inside it the shake has full power. powerPoly Required power. durationPoly Required duration in seconds. width is a diameter and search.radius is a radius. A circle that telegraphs a radius: 1000 blast is width: 2000. Nothing checks this.

The four retired slots are rejected as node types. Use the alternatives below. Name Say instead COST upkeep: on the node that raises the affect. SPLASH collect: { search: ... }. CURSE A TICKER with attach: affect and counters:. DPS A TICKER with attach: affect.

handler: names an entry in <vnum>.lua, which returns a table of handlers. A handler implements any of gate, damage_intent or applied. gate can veto the node, damage_intent reshapes a hit before defence, applied runs after an affect landed. A declared handler with no Lua file, a handler name the file does not contain, or a handler with none of the three functions is logged and the node stays inert.

A binding connects a trait definition to an affect type. A definition can have several bindings. Every binding for a type opens when any caller adds an affect of that type, and closes when the last affect of that type is removed.

Door How Skill loader A C++ loader reads traits: entries on an affect-raising skill node. Lua forge.sys.game.traits.bind(id, affect_type, formulas); define with gate calls this as shorthand. A skill, a mode, or a consumable item that adds the bound affect can open the gate. Equipping gear cannot: equipment applies points through ApplyPoint, not AddAffect. A point with the same number as an affect type is not a gate.

The example binds a named formula, then primes its constant immediately before adding the affect. Choose an unused affect ID; see affect type IDs. local traits = forge.sys.game.traits traits["define"]{ id = "ward", hooks = { on_damage_taken_final = function(ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) local pct = ctx.formula("reduction", 0, { dam = ctx.damage }) pct = math.max(0, math.min(pct, 100)) ctx.damage = ctx.damage * (1 - pct / 100) end, }, } affect.add_name_definition("EXAMPLE_WARD", 3901) affect.add_no_save(affect.name_map.EXAMPLE_WARD) local binding = traits.bind("ward", affect.name_map.EXAMPLE_WARD, { reduction = "power*5" }) local function apply_ward(ch, power) if binding == 0 then return false end ch:remove_affect(affect.name_map.EXAMPLE_WARD) traits.prime_constants(ch, binding, { power = power }) ch:add_affect(affect.name_map.EXAMPLE_WARD, point.NONE, 0, 0, 600, 0, true) return true end

A node that raises an affect takes a list of entries. The gate is its affect, or the skill vnum if none is named. - type: AFFECT id: example_node traits: - id: ward constants: { power: skill_level } formulas: { reduction: "power*5" } point: PHYSICAL_RESISTANCE params names end in _point, _column, or _affect and resolve to enum integers. Constants must use the skill formula vocabulary. Use traits: as a list, never singular trait:; put constants, formulas, and params inside each entry.

Formulas and constants are frozen for a character's node at the gate. The skill loader primes constants before adding the affect; Lua can do the same with prime_constants. Remove an old affect before priming: closing its gate clears constants. Reapplying an active affect normally renews duration without another activation. Closing the gate clears counters, cooldowns, schedules, and constants; state is cleared unless keep_state_on_deactivate is set. Activation resets counters and enables the trait. Constants are session-scoped. A restored affect opens without them; use the affect value through ctx.gate_value() for durable data, or use a no-save affect. Rebinding the same trait and affect pair replaces formulas and returns the same binding ID. unbind removes it from the affect index; existing active nodes continue until their gate closes. bind returns 0 for an unknown ID. Definitions must exist before a Lua bind. If several affects share a type, gate_value() reads the first one. For the C++ registration interface, see native traits.

A trait gives a character behavior while a bound affect is present. Use one for a condition, a counter, or a change at a formula position. For an unconditional flat point bonus, use an affect point. A definition describes behavior. A binding associates that definition with an affect type and formulas. Adding an affect of that type opens the gate; removing the last one closes it. See Traits foundations for the model.

Term Meaning Definition The trait's ID, hooks, stage, and counter declarations. Binding An association between a definition and an affect type, with named formulas. Gate The presence of an affect of a bound type on a character. Hook A callback invoked for a subscribed event or position. Transform hook A hook that can change the damage or heal being computed. Observer hook A hook that observes an event without changing its computed value. ctx The per-character, per-binding context for state and operations. Stage Ascending order among traits at a staged formula position. Formula position A point in an engine calculation or decision where traits participate. Bump point Temporarily add to a character point during a guarded damage computation. Trigger mask Bits identifying the events a trait subscribes to. Forge The environment that loads and runs the Lua definition. Native trait A C++ implementation registered with the native registry. Lua trait A definition and hooks registered through Forge Lua.

Define a trait: hooks, context, counters, and bumps. Stage and formula positions: ordering and reachable positions. Bind a trait: connect a definition to an affect. Register a native trait: C++ registration and point limits. Examples and pitfalls: small recipes and common traps.

A native trait is a stateless INativeTrait singleton. Register its class with REGISTER_NATIVE_TRAIT; hook macros declare the override and its trigger bit together. Per-character data belongs to the trait node, reached through ctx.pkTraits and ctx.bindingId.

Operation Interface Identity, order, counters TRAIT_ID, TRAIT_STAGE, TRAIT_COUNTERS Hooks TRAIT_ON_* macros; targeting uses TRAIT_BLOCKS_TARGETING Register REGISTER_NATIVE_TRAIT(Class) at static initialization Bind CCharTraitsManager::instance().BindTrait(id, affect, formulas, &created) Unbind UnbindTrait(binding_id) Prime constants ch->Traits().PrimeConstants(binding, values) Registration defines behavior; it does not open a gate. The skill loader binds native traits through BindTrait. Lua forge.sys.game.traits.bind is the second binding door. See binding. BindTrait resolves native IDs before Lua definitions, returns 0 for an unknown ID, and reuses a binding for the same ID and affect type, replacing formulas. created distinguishes a new binding from a reused one; only release a binding your code created. Duplicate native IDs are rejected. A registration without hooks is logged. Native hooks are const. ctx.Formula, ctx.Constant, ctx.GateValue(), and ctx.EndSelf() access binding data. Native ctx.Formula supplies dam from ctx.iDamage in a transform and zero elsewhere. Transform contexts carry mutable ctx.iDamage, ctx.iDamageType, and ctx.wSkillVnum.

TRAIT_POINT_LIMIT supplies an upper cap for a point while the trait is active. Return 0 for no opinion. The highest claim wins; stage does not order this operation. It cannot lower a cap and has no context or Lua equivalent. See formula positions for the positions reachable from Lua.

Define a trait once per process from a game Forge environment. A definition may include gate as shorthand for a Lua binding; otherwise bind it separately. Restart the game cores after changing a definition. forge.sys.game.traits["define"]{ id = "ward", hooks = { on_damage_taken_final = function(ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) ctx.damage = ctx.damage * 0.9 end, }, }

Field Type Meaning id string, required The name every other call uses. gate { affect = <affect type> }, optional Binds to this affect immediately. Without it, the trait stays unbound until a skill node or bind binds it. stage integer, default 0 Order among traits that share one formula position, ascending. See stage ordering. counters list, optional A plain string is a manual counter. { name = "dealt", accumulate = "DAMAGE_DEALT_POST" } also fills itself. keep_state_on_deactivate boolean, default false Keep ctx.state when the gate closes. hooks table, optional The behaviour. Each hook you declare subscribes the trait to its trigger. A def with no hooks and no accumulating counters is never dispatched. A misspelled hook name is not an error. Only the 24 known names are read.

An accumulate counter is incremented by the engine without a Lua call. What a counter gains per trigger is fixed by the trigger, not inferred from the value: Trigger Gain per event DAMAGE_DEALT_POST, DAMAGE_TAKEN_POST the dam of the post hook, never below 0 (see the post hooks) HEAL_DONE, HEAL_TAKEN the heal amount, never below 0 KILL, DIED, TICK_1HZ, SKILL_CAST, DEBUFF_GIVEN, DEBUFF_TAKEN, BUFF_GIVEN, BUFF_TAKEN 1 The other trigger names are accepted by the parser and never count, see pitfalls. An unknown accumulate string logs an error and the counter is added as manual-only.

define returns 0 after the first four. The two counter errors log and go on defining. Log line Cause [traits] define: missing id The table has no id. [traits] define: duplicate id [{}] The id is already defined in this process. [traits] define [{}]: a native trait already owns this id A C++ trait registered the id. [traits] define [{}]: gate is present but gate.affect is 0 For example affect.name_map.X is nil. [traits] define [{}]: unknown accumulate [{}] The counter exists, manual only. [traits] define [{}]: counter without name That counter is skipped.

Every per-character function takes a trait name (the id of the def) and resolves it to this character's binding in this order: the active binding of that def, else any node of that def, else the def's first binding. If the character has no trait data at all, the call is a no-op that returns 0, false or nothing. Function Signature Returns What it does define define(def) dense def id (> 0), or 0 on failure Registers a def. With gate, it also binds at once, with no formulas. Logs [OK] [traits] define [id] id=.. affect_gate=.. binding=.. hook_mask=0x... Errors are under define errors. bind bind(trait_id, affect_type, formulas?) binding id, or 0 Gates a trait on an affect with this binding's formulas. Each formula string is analysed; a bad one logs [traits] bind [id]: cannot analyze formula [name]: 'expr' and is kept empty. An unknown trait id returns 0 with no log line. Binding the same (trait, affect) pair again returns the same id with the formulas replaced. unbind unbind(binding_id) nothing Takes the binding out of the affect index. Characters already holding it keep working until their gate closes. Binding the same pair again re-indexes it. prime_constants prime_constants(ch, binding_id, values) nothing Gives the character's node the constants of the binding. Only string keys with number values are kept, the rest are skipped silently. It replaces the node's whole constants map. is_active is_active(ch, trait_id) boolean The gate is open and the trait is not disabled. counter counter(ch, trait_id, name) number The counter value, 0 for an unknown counter, trait or character. add_counter add_counter(ch, trait_id, name, delta) number Adds delta and returns the new value. delta is an unsigned 64-bit value: do not use it to decrement, use set_counter. set_counter set_counter(ch, trait_id, name, value) nothing Overwrites a counter. reset_counters reset_counters(ch, trait_id) nothing Zeroes every counter, keeps the state. reset_state reset_state(ch, trait_id) nothing Only if active. Cancels schedules, clears cooldowns, zeroes counters, gives a fresh ctx.state and runs on_activate again. Constants are kept. set_cooldown set_cooldown(ch, trait_id, name, seconds) nothing Starts or restarts a named cooldown. The deadline is whole seconds, rounded up. cooldown_remaining cooldown_remaining(ch, trait_id, name) number Seconds left, 0 if expired or never set. is_on_cooldown is_on_cooldown(ch, trait_id, name) boolean cooldown_remaining > 0. clear_cooldown clear_cooldown(ch, trait_id, name) nothing Drops a cooldown at once. schedule schedule(ch, trait_id, name, seconds) nothing A one-shot delayed callback to on_scheduled(ch, name, ctx). A pending schedule of the same name is cancelled first. The minimum delay is one pulse. cancel_scheduled cancel_scheduled(ch, trait_id, name) nothing No-op if none is pending. is_scheduled is_scheduled(ch, trait_id, name) boolean A schedule with this name is pending. disable disable(ch, trait_id) nothing Only if active. Hooks and auto-accumulation stop. State, counters and the affect stay. enable enable(ch, trait_id) nothing Resumes a disabled trait. is_disabled is_disabled(ch, trait_id) boolean disable_all disable_all(ch) nothing Disables every active trait on the character. enable_all enable_all(ch) nothing Enables every disabled trait on the character.
Lifecycle hooks manage activation and schedules; pre hooks support point bumps; transform hooks change a value; post and event hooks observe. See stage and positions for ordering.

Each hook you declare adds its trigger bit to the trait's mask. on_activate, on_deactivate and on_scheduled add no bit. In every signature ch is the character the trait is attached to and ctx is that character's ctx for this binding. Where a character may be absent, the argument is nil. Hook Arguments Fires when on_activate (ch, ctx) The gate goes from closed to open. Counters are already zeroed and constants already primed. on_deactivate (ch, ctx) The gate closes, and again when the character object is destroyed. In the destruction case the ctx functions do nothing, ch is still valid. on_scheduled (ch, name, ctx) A schedule deadline elapsed. on_damage_dealt_pre (ch, victim, dam_type, ctx) Before the damage formula reads the attacker's points. Bump points here. on_damage_taken_pre (ch, attacker, dam_type, ctx) The victim side of the same moment. attacker can be nil. on_damage_dealt_post (ch, victim, dam, dam_type, ctx) After the hit. dam is the amount the damage formula handed to the victim, before the victim-side transforms and the critical and pierce adjustments that follow, so it is not the health the victim lost. Observe only. on_damage_taken_post (ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) The same for the victim. attacker can be nil. on_damage_taken_raw (ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) Transform, before defense. on_damage_taken_final (ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) Transform, after the damage amplifiers. on_damage_dealt_final (ch, victim, dam, dam_type, ctx) Attacker-side transform at the same point, before the victim's final transforms. on_hit_resolved (ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, damage_flag, ctx) The resolved hit, with the critical and pierce bits in damage_flag. Observe only, but ctx.end_self() is valid here: the trait may close its gate here. on_attack (ch, ctx) ch threw an attack motion, any attack, hit or not. on_target_scan (ch, finder, ctx) returns boolean finder is acquiring a target. Return true to hide ch from it. on_kill (ch, victim, ctx) ch landed the killing blow. on_died (ch, attacker, ctx) ch died. attacker can be nil. on_tick (ch, ctx) Once a second while the gate is open. Declaring it enrols the character in the global one-second walk. on_skill_cast (ch, skill_vnum, ctx) ch cast a skill that passed the validity checks, before the cooldown and cost checks, so a cast refused for cooldown or cost still fires it. Filter on skill_vnum. on_debuff_given (ch, target, affect_type, ctx) ch landed a bad affect on target. on_debuff_taken (ch, attacker, affect_type, ctx) The counterpart. attacker can be nil for quest or environment debuffs. on_buff_given (ch, target, affect_type, ctx) ch applied a good affect to target. on_buff_taken (ch, source, affect_type, ctx) ch received one. source can be nil. on_heal_done (ch, target, amount, ctx) ch delivered a skill heal. Regeneration and potions have no healer and fire nothing here. on_heal_taken_pre (ch, healer, amount, source, ctx) Transform, before a received heal lands. source is a forge.sys.game.HEAL_SOURCE, documented with the forge.sys.game namespace. on_heal_taken (ch, healer, amount, ctx) ch gained health by any route. healer is always nil. dam_type is a forge.sys.game.DAMAGE_TYPE value. In a transform hook, dam is only a convenience copy: read and write ctx.damage. The transform hooks run for every hit the victim takes, damage-over-time ticks and reflected damage included, while the two pre hooks run only at the three bump sites. Filter on dam_type (POISON, BLEEDING) when a reduction must not touch ticks. The dam of the post hooks is the amount handed to the victim, so a reduction written in a transform hook does not show in it. Every Lua hook is called through a protected call. An error logs [traits] <hook> [<trait id>]: <lua error> and the engine carries on. on_scheduled adds name=[<name>] before the colon, and an on_deactivate that fails at character destruction is logged as [traits] ~CCharTraits on_deactivate [<trait id>]: <lua error>. A transform hook that errors leaves the damage or the heal unchanged. An on_target_scan that errors leaves the owner visible.

A ctx is built once per activation, per character and binding. Two skills that gate the same trait give a character two independent ctxs, with their own counters, cooldowns, state and numbers. A ctx kept beyond the character's life turns every function into a no-op, and the cached ctx is dropped on every activation, deactivation and reset_state.

Field Hooks Meaning ctx.state all Per-character and binding Lua scratch table. It lives until on_deactivate, or across gate flips with keep_state_on_deactivate. ctx.damage on_damage_taken_raw, on_damage_taken_final, on_damage_dealt_final Pre-filled with the damage and read back when the hook returns. The value is rounded and clamped at 0. A non-number, or a field left untouched, leaves the damage alone. ctx.skill_vnum the same three transform hooks Read-only. The skill that dealt the hit; 0 for a basic attack, a damage-over-time tick or a reflect. A cast with no performer still names its skill. ctx.amount on_heal_taken_pre Pre-filled with the incoming heal, read back the same way as ctx.damage.

Function Meaning ctx.counter(name), ctx.add_counter(name, delta), ctx.set_counter(name, value), ctx.reset_counters() The counter functions in the trait API, for this binding. add_counter returns the new value. ctx.bump_point(point, delta) Adds delta to a point of ch, the holder, for the rest of the damage formula. Meant for the two pre hooks only, see bump points. ctx.set_cooldown, ctx.cooldown_remaining, ctx.is_on_cooldown, ctx.clear_cooldown The cooldown functions, for this binding. ctx.schedule, ctx.cancel_scheduled, ctx.is_scheduled The schedule functions. The framework owns the event and cancels it on deactivate and on character destruction. ctx.since_activation() Seconds since the gate opened. ctx.is_active() True inside hooks except during teardown. ctx.formula(name, fallback, vars?) Evaluates a named formula of this binding. See Formulas and constants. ctx.constant(name, fallback) A number the binding froze when the affect landed. ctx.gate_value() The gating affect's own value. If several affects of that type are up, the first counts. ctx.end_self() Removes the affect that gates this trait, so the normal expiry path deactivates it. A trait never removes its own affect by hand.

A binding carries named formulas (strings in the formula language of the skill files) and the character's node carries constants (numbers). ctx.formula(name, fallback, vars?) evaluates one formula as follows: All variables are cleared. The node's constants are set by name. amount is set to the gate value. The names in vars are set. dam is not special on this path. A formula that names dam gets it only when you pass dam = ... in vars. A name nobody supplies logs once per binding and formula, [traits] formula [{}] on binding {} references [{}], which neither the gate's constants nor the call site supply - using the fallback, and the call returns the fallback. A binding with no such formula, or an empty one, returns the fallback silently, so always pass a working default. A constant is a number the binder resolved in its own vocabulary and froze when the affect landed, for example a caster's skill level. Anything you can read at hook time is a variable: pass it in vars, or a frozen value is used forever.

ctx.bump_point(point, delta) temporarily changes the holder's point. Use it in on_damage_dealt_pre or on_damage_taken_pre; the guard unwinds bumps when the damage computation ends. Bumps add together, and nested guards unwind independently. Guarded site dam_type Melee basic attack NORMAL Ranged shot or magic weapon basic attack NORMAL_RANGE or NORMAL_MAGIC Skill damage node The node's declared type Filter by damage type when the bonus is limited to one delivery. A splash skill can calculate its amount once for multiple victims, so do not use a victim-dependent attacker bump for it. A bump outside a guard is ignored; a later hook can run inside a guard but its bump lasts until that guard ends. Use a transform for changing damage there. Normal point reads include bumps. The limit-clamped reads used by skill formulas for MOV_SPEED, CRITICAL_PCT, ATT_SPEED, CASTING_SPEED, and IQ do not. Next: Stage and formula positions.

A stage orders traits at a staged formula position. Each transform receives the previous transform's output. Declare stage on a Lua definition or TRAIT_STAGE(n) on a native trait; the default is 0.

This invented chain shares one final damage position: Stage Trait Order 0 ward_a First 10 ward_b Second 20 bonus_c Third Native and Lua traits interleave in ascending stage order. Within a stage, character nodes run in creation order. A trait attached during dispatch does not run in that round. Target scanning stops when a trait hides the owner. Stage applies to on_damage_taken_raw, on_damage_taken_final, on_damage_dealt_final, on_heal_taken_pre, on_hit_resolved, on_attack, and on_target_scan. Other hooks ignore stage: native nodes run first, then Lua nodes, each in node order.

Position Lua hook Effect Attacker damage intent on_damage_dealt_pre Bump points inside the guard. Victim damage intent on_damage_taken_pre Bump points inside the guard. Before defense on_damage_taken_raw Change ctx.damage. After amplifiers, attacker on_damage_dealt_final Change ctx.damage before victim transforms. After amplifiers, victim on_damage_taken_final Change ctx.damage. Resolved hit on_hit_resolved Observe damage and flags; may end the gate. Attack motion on_attack Observe; may end the gate. Target acquisition on_target_scan Return true to hide the holder. Received heal on_heal_taken_pre Change ctx.amount. Point limit None Native-only TRAIT_POINT_LIMIT raises an upper cap. The damage intent hooks are guarded bump sites, but are not stage ordered. Lua reaches the other positions in the table except point limit. Transform damage is rounded and clamped at zero. See hooks and native registration.

The loader renders a template in one of two ways. A debug client parses the template source each time; a production client runs a precompiled Python module and ignores the source text. Debug client Production client Source file Opened and rendered Opened, then not used for rendering Jinja environment Fresh per render, so edits show on reload Cached for the process Compiled module Not used Required

The loader takes the compiled path when all of these hold: the client is not a debug client; the host called UseCompiledTemplate() on the loader; the template path starts with the path the host's resolver returns for "", so the loader can derive a template name from the rest. The module is looked up as tmpl/tmpl_<sha1 of the template name>.py through the host's path resolver, from the pack first. A missing module raises a template-not-found error.

Load always opens the template file first, through the pack and then the folder, even when it will render from the module. A compiled module alone does not satisfy that read: ship the .html with its module. LoadString takes the text directly and has no such read.

Precompiling is the host's build step. The wiki has one in its Wiki Manager. A cached compiled environment keeps the path resolver it was created with, so a resolver changed after the first render is not seen.

With ENABLE_WIKI_DEV on, the loader validates the template source before rendering. The validator strips Jinja directives and expressions, uses placeholder tags for macro boundaries, and checks the remaining HTML. Errors stop the load and log HTML Validation Errors in template source:. A valid source does not guarantee that every render produces the layout you meant.

These examples define behavior. Bind each definition to an affect as shown in binding.

forge.sys.game.traits["define"]{ id = "example_reduction", hooks = { on_damage_taken_final = function(ch, attacker, dam, dam_type, ctx) ctx.damage = ctx.damage * 0.7 end, }, } This transform includes damage-over-time and reflected damage. Filter dam_type when those should be excluded.

forge.sys.game.traits["define"]{ id = "example_counter", counters = { { name = "dealt", accumulate = "DAMAGE_DEALT_POST" } }, hooks = { on_tick = function(ch, ctx) if ctx.counter("dealt") > 1000 then ctx.reset_counters() end end, }, } The post amount is the amount handed to the victim before victim-side transforms and later critical and pierce adjustments, not necessarily health lost.

documents.t: Symptom Cause and fix Equipping a point does not activate a trait Equipment uses ApplyPoint, not AddAffect. Add the bound affect to open the gate. A bump does nothing or lasts too long Use it only in the two damage pre hooks. Other hooks may be outside the guard or run inside one that outlives the hook. A bump reaches unintended attacks Filter dam_type; the same pre hooks cover melee, ranged, and skill damage. A formula uses its fallback Pass live variables such as dam in vars; check that the named formula and constants exist. A restored affect has no constants Constants are session-scoped. Use ctx.gate_value() for durable values or a no-save affect. A hook never fires Unknown hook names are ignored. Check the spelling and the definition's logged mask. A counter stays at zero Only the triggers listed under automatic counters feed counters. Other recognized trigger names do not. A Lua bind returns 0 Define the ID before binding and check the return value. A scheduled callback outlives its trait Use ctx.schedule; it is cancelled on deactivation and destruction. Do not retain a ctx in an external closure. A disabled trait starts running again Opening its gate enables it. Disable it again if required. A fractional cooldown lasts longer than expected Cooldowns round up to whole seconds. A teardown callback cannot use ctx functions At character destruction ch remains valid, but ctx functions are inert. See definition and hooks and Traits foundations.

The UCHTML Grid System is inspired by traditional HTML/CSS layout techniques and adapted for Metin2's native UI elements. It follows a two-pass layout process: Measure Pass Each UIElement calculates the required dimensions based on its attributes and content. Properties such as width, height, margin, and padding determine the space needed by the element and its children. Layout Pass After computing sizes, each element is positioned within its parent container. The layout process respects margins, paddings, and alignment rules, ensuring elements are placed correctly according to their defined display mode. UIElements serve as the core building blocks by encapsulating both appearance and behavior, and they are directly mapped to native Metin2 UI components.

The table below summarizes the primary attributes available in the UCHTML Grid System: Attribute Type Allowed Values / Default Description id String N/A Unique identifier for the element, used for anchoring (# url segment). display String "block" (default), "flex", "relative" Determines layout mode: block (vertical stacking), flex (multi-line horizontal flow), or relative (explicit positioning). margin Number or CSS-like shorthand N/A Sets external spacing; supports shorthand (e.g., margin-x, margin-y, margin-top, etc.). padding Number or CSS-like shorthand N/A Sets internal spacing; supports shorthand similar to margin. width Number, "auto", "content", or percentage N/A Defines the element’s width. "content" defers to child elements; "auto" fills available space. height Number, "auto", "content", or percentage N/A Defines the element’s height. "content" defers to child elements; "auto" fills available space. max-width DISABLED Number or percentage string N/A Ignored: the loader reads no max-width. max-height Number or percentage string N/A Maximum allowed height; clamps the computed height if exceeded. align String "left" (default), "center", "right" Horizontal alignment within the container (applies to non-flex layouts). vertical-align String "top" (default), "center", "bottom" Vertical alignment within the container (applies to non-flex layouts). x Number N/A X-coordinate for positioning; used with relative display mode. y Number N/A Y-coordinate for positioning; used with relative display mode. spacing Number N/A Vertical gap between flex lines when using flex display mode. justify-content String "flex-start" (default), "flex-end", "center", "space-between", "space-around", "space-evenly" Controls horizontal distribution in flex layout. align-items String "flex-start" (default), "flex-end", "center", "stretch" Controls vertical alignment within each flex line. name String N/A Optional name for the element; often used for setting window names or identifiers.
UCHTML supports three primary display modes that determine how elements are arranged and interact:
Elements with display="block" are arranged in a vertical stack. They honor margins and paddings, and the container size is influenced by the cumulative dimensions of its children. Example:

With display="flex", elements are laid out horizontally in rows. Items wrap to a new line if there isn’t enough space. This mode supports additional properties such as justify-content and align-items for precise control over distribution and alignment.

Value Description flex-start Items align to the beginning (left) of the container. This is the default setting, placing all items flush against the start edge. flex-end Items align to the end (right) of the container, causing leftover space to appear at the beginning (left) of the container. center Items are centered horizontally within the container, with equal space distributed on both sides. space-between Items are evenly distributed; the first item is at the start, the last at the end, and the remaining space is divided equally between the items. space-around Items are evenly distributed with equal space around them. The space on the edges is half the size of the space between items. space-evenly Items are distributed with equal spacing between them, including equal space at the container edges.

Value Description flex-start Items align to the top of the flex line. This is the default setting, aligning items flush with the top edge. flex-end Items align to the bottom of the flex line, placing them flush with the bottom edge. center Items are centered vertically within the flex line, ensuring equal spacing above and below each item. stretch Items stretch to fill the entire height of the flex line (while respecting margins), which may override the individual height of the items. Example: In this example the Child elements are placed one near the other putting the same space between them. Elements in the same row are then certically aligned at the center (therefore smaller elements are in the middle of the row)
Elements with display="relative" are positioned using explicit x and y coordinates. This mode allows an element to be placed independently of the normal document flow. Example:

Sizing is a critical aspect of the grid system. UCHTML provides various methods to define an element’s dimensions: Numeric Values: Specify fixed sizes directly (e.g., width="300" sets the width to 300 pixels). auto: The element expands to fill the available space in its container, minus any margins. With "available space" we mean container's specified dimension minus the space occupied by already placed elements, keep in mind that the root element has size equals to the window containing the UCHTML loader content: The element’s size is derived from the dimensions of its child elements, allowing the container to adapt to its content. Percentage Values: Sizes can be expressed as a percentage (e.g., width="50%") of the parent container’s dimensions. Calculations take into account the parent's size and any applied margins. Max Constraints: max-height clamps the computed height. max-width is disabled: the loader never reads it, so it has no effect. Example: In this example the div will occopy half of the container width and all the remaining vertical space of the container with a max of 300.
When using percentage values, the computed dimensions adjust dynamically based on the parent container's size and applied margins.

Jinja2 is a modern, designer-friendly templating engine for Python. It is used to generate dynamic web content, such as HTML, XML, or other text-based formats. Jinja2 makes it easy to separate business logic from presentation logic by providing a rich set of features including variable interpolation, control structures, and template inheritance. In the context of UCHTML, Jinja2 works together with HTML to greatly enhance the expressivity of the system, allowing developers to embed backend functions and create reactive interfaces. For a full reference, see the official Jinja2 documentation.
Define variables within the template to be used later. Example: {% set title = "Welcome to the task board" %}

Insert variable values or evaluate expressions directly into the HTML output. Example:

{{ title }}

Create reusable template fragments that can be invoked with different parameters. First you define a macro: `{% macro macro_name(parameters) %} ... {% endmacro %}` Tehn you can call a macro: {{ macro_name(arguments) }} Example: {% macro render_header(text) %}

{{ text }}

{% endmacro %} {{ render_header("My Page Title") }}
Embed the contents of one template into another, promoting modularity. Example: {% include "templates/footer.html" %}

Build upon a base template by overriding defined blocks, facilitating template inheritance. Example: Base Template Example (base.html): {% block title %}Default Title{% endblock %}
{% block content %} {% endblock %}
{% block footer %}

Footer content here

{% endblock %}
{% extends "base.html" %} {% block content %}

This is my custom content.

{% endblock %}

Invoke backend or custom Python functions within the template. Functions are passed via the template context. {% set user_name = get_user_name(user_id) %}

Welcome, {{ user_name }}!

A task board with two tabs. The tab variable comes from the host, and the filter group writes it back when the player picks a tab. {% import "templates/headers.html" as header %} {% set tab = fun.getv("tab", "open") %} {% set tasks = fun.getv("tasks", []) %} <main> <filter-group type="tabs" filter-target="tab" width="auto" default="open"> <filter type="tab" height="25" width="100" padding="5" filter-value="open"> <txt align="center">Open</txt> </filter> {% if fun.notempty(tasks) %} <filter type="tab" height="25" width="100" padding="5" filter-value="all"> <txt align="center">All</txt> </filter> {% endif %} </filter-group> {% if tab == "open" %} {{ header.h2("Open tasks") }} {% for task in tasks if not task.done %} <bullet-list margin-bottom="5">{{ task.name }}</bullet-list> {% else %} <txt>Nothing left to do.</txt> {% endfor %} {% endif %} {% if tab == "all" %} {{ header.h2("All tasks") }} <lazy-div preload="15" display="flex" width="auto" spacing="5"> {% for task in tasks %} <txt width="48%">{{ task.name }}</txt> {% endfor %} </lazy-div> {% endif %} </main> Part What it does import ... as header Loads macros from another template through the loader's path resolver. header.h2 is a macro defined there. fun.getv("tab", "open") Reads a variable the host or a filter group set, with a default. See the context. fun.notempty(tasks) Shows the second tab only when there is something to list. filter-group type="tabs" Writes the picked filter-value into the variable named by filter-target; the page re-renders with the new value. See filter groups. {% if tab == ... %} Selects the content for the active tab. Everything outside the branch is not built. lazy-div Queues children beyond preload so a long list does not freeze the client. Updates that should not rebuild the page belong in reactive zones.

Every template renders against a context dictionary. The loader fills it before each load, then merges the variables the host passes in, so a host value replaces a standard entry of the same name. Name Provided by Reference fun the loader below bonus the loader below interfacemodule, i18n, world, item, mob, quest a client that loads game data the wiki data namespaces any other name the host, as injected_variables A host adds a namespace by passing a dictionary of values or callables to Load or LoadString; a template calls them like the built-ins.

Name: getv Parameters: key: (String) The key to retrieve from the context. default: (Optional) The default value to return if the key is not found. Return: The value associated with the key after processing by the var function. Call Example: {% set value = fun.getv("query:example", "default_value") %}

Name: getvi Parameters: key: (String) The key to retrieve from the context. default: (Optional, default=0) The default value if the key is not found. Return: An integer value converted from the retrieved variable. Call Example: {% set number = fun.getvi("query:number", 10) %}

Name: setv Parameters: key: (String) The key to set in the context. value: The value to store; processed via the var function. reload: (Boolean, default=True) Determines whether to trigger a page reload after setting the variable. Return: None (Updates the context and may trigger a reload). Call Example: {% set _ = fun.setv("user:status", "active") %}

Name: var Parameters: data: The data to process. default: (Optional) A default value used if data is not provided. Return: The processed data, where: If data is a string starting with "packed_query:", it is replaced by the named list the host configures (the wiki reads them from PACKED_QUERY). If data is a comma-separated string, it is split into a list. If default is a list or tuple and data is not, data is converted into a list. Call Example: {% set processed = fun.var("1,2,3", []) %}

The in-game wiki is a client built on UCHTML: pages are templates, and the facts they show are generated offline from the server's files. The framework pages (layout, Jinja2, generic tags) live under UCHTML; these pages cover what the wiki adds. Page What it covers Quickstart Create and open a page Configuration config.yaml, whitelists and locale binding URL format wiki:// addresses, query parameters and location Data generation The Wiki Manager and its outputs Data namespaces: i18n, quest, mob Template functions for names, quests and mobs Data namespace: item Template functions for items Data namespace: world Higher-level item, mob, cube and refine queries Item and equipment tags Data-bound item, equipment and cube tags Monster and chest tags Data-bound monster and chest tags Shop and ranking tags Tags for the item shop and ranking clients

A reactive zone is a div or body that rebuilds its children when a variable it watches changes, and keeps the rest of the page and its scroll position as they are. For the mechanism behind it, read UCHTML in Foundations.

A div or body becomes a zone when the loader has reactive handling enabled and the tag has a parent, a nonempty id and a nonempty reactive attribute. Attribute Requirement Meaning id Required Identifies the zone in the re-rendered page. Unique within the loader. reactive Required Comma-separated variable names the zone watches, without spaces.
{% set step_done = fun.getvi('step_done', 0) %} {% set step_need = fun.getvi('step_need', 0) %} Progress: {{ step_done }}/{{ step_need }}
Read the watched variables inside the zone with fun.getv or fun.getvi. Inside a zone every Jinja2 feature works: conditionals, loops, macros and filters.

Call loader.SetVar("step_done", 15) for one variable, or loader.SetVars({"step_done": 15, "step_need": 20}) to change several with one update for all affected zones. reload=False on SetVar updates the context and calls the variable callback without any rebuild.

The loader finds the zones watching the changed keys. It renders the whole template again. For each affected zone it finds the zone by id in the new result, destroys the zone's old children and builds new ones from the new result. The zone root is marked dirty and its parent is told of the change. There is no diff: the engine has a tree differ and stores virtual trees, but this path never calls it. The cost of an update therefore scales with the size of the template and of the zone, not with how much changed. A zone saves the layout and construction of the rest of the tree, not the Jinja render.

The loader reloads the whole page, preserving scroll, when: no zone watches the changed variable; a zone update fails, including when its id is missing from the re-rendered result; in a batch, any changed key is unwatched or a watching zone cannot take the reactive path. Nested zones that watch different variables update in no specified order.

Use a zone for Use a full reload for Counters, progress bars, status text Layout changes and tab switches that change the page structure A list that changes inside one container Initial load Anything that updates often Variables no zone watches (automatic) Keep zones small and focused on their variables. One zone around the whole page rebuilds everything and gains nothing.

Wiki pages never carry game facts by hand. Item, mob, shop, refine, cube and quest facts are generated offline from the server's own files into static JSON that the client reads from its pack. A page asks for them through the item, mob, quest and world namespaces of the template context. The tool that generates and edits all of this is the Wiki Manager, a desktop application (PyQt) with one tab per task.

The builder reads the server's side of the game: Source Gives item_proto.txt, mob_proto.txt, mob_adaptive_proto.txt in the prototypes folder Items and mobs. group.txt, group_group.txt, cube.txt in the server locale folder Mob groups and crafting recipes. The server locale's shop and refine data, its map folder and the regen folders for cron, domain, event and dungeon data Shops, refines and spawns. The interpreted quests Drops, spawns, rewards and quest records that only exist inside quest scripts.

Quest scripts are Lua programs, so their rewards and spawns cannot be read like a table. The Wiki Manager's Interpreter tab reads each quest script, expands the reward tables, and asks a language model (an OpenAI-compatible chat API, configured with a provider, a model and a key in the tab) to return one JSON record for it: quest type, maps and spawns, drops, rewards, reward choices, involved mobs and items, primary NPC, minimum level, unlocked quests and questline. The prompt tells the model to leave a field out when the script does not state it and to ignore commented-out code. The records are saved as one JSON file per quest in the interpreted quest folder. The builder reads that folder; it never calls the model. You run the interpreter again only for quests that changed, and you review the resulting records like any other generated data.

A build writes six files into the wiki folder (locale/[localization]/wiki): File Holds items.json Items: refines, shops, drops, chests, quests, crafts. mobs.json Mobs: drops, spawns, shops, crafts, kill rewards. cube.json Crafting recipes. refine_trees.json Upgrade chains. refine_sets.json Refine material sets. quests.json Quest records, read through the quest namespace. and two reports into the builder's own build folder, mobs_by_map.json and mobs_without_map.json, which list the spawn data per map and the mobs that no map reaches.

items_ex.json and mobs_ex.json live next to the generated files and are written by hand, never by the builder. The client deep-merges them over items.json and mobs.json when it loads, so use them for data the pipeline does not capture. A rebuild overwrites items.json and mobs.json, and leaves the _ex files alone.

The paths of a build are the prototypes folder, the server locale folder, the interpreted quest folder and the output folder. The Wiki Manager's Builder tab shows the defaults and lets you override each one; the same four can be set through the environment variables WIKI_BUILDER_PROTO_PATH, WIKI_BUILDER_LOCALE_PATH, WIKI_BUILDER_INTERPRETED_QUEST_PATH and WIKI_BUILDER_OUTPUT_PATH. Install the Wiki Manager requirements (PyQt, ruamel.yaml, PyYAML, lupa, and openai for the Interpreter tab) in a virtual environment. Start the Wiki Manager and open the Builder tab. Check the paths and run the builder. It runs eight numbered steps: quests, cubes, shops, refines, items, mobs, quest records, then merge and write. Pack the generated files with the other wiki files.

The other tabs edit the files described in configuration without touching their comments: map info, quest, raid and dungeon names, packed queries, locale strings, origin mappings, indexed pages, search result categories, wiki categories and whitelists.

The Compiler tab compiles every .html and .jinja page under the wiki folder into a Python module named tmpl_<hash of the page name>.py in wiki/tmpl. A client that is not a debug client renders pages from these modules and never reads the .html source, so recompile after every page change that must reach players. Clean + Compile removes the existing compiled files first, which drops modules of pages you deleted.
Native registrant What it registers The data pipeline is Python and JSON on both sides; nothing is registered in C++.

The wiki loads generated game data and registers it in every template context next to the fun and bonus namespaces. Facts are generated offline by the Wiki Manager; item and world namespaces have their own pages.
The interfacemodule object provides access to all interfaceModule functions, this object is ment for advanced internal use and needs knoewldge over the Python code handling the game interface.

Name: t Parameters: key: The key to translate. Return: The text for key.
